-- Frontline roster. csn_hr is not accessible, so columns that only exist there
-- are REMOVED rather than written blank.
--
-- WHY THE EMPLOYEE KEY IS COALESCED: a diagnostic run on 2026-09-11 showed
-- COUNT(DISTINCT emid) = 0 across all 128,694 'Day' rows - emid is NULL for
-- every row in this table. A previous version filtered on emid IS NOT NULL and
-- therefore returned nothing. The key below falls back through emailaddress,
-- username and employee, so the roster works whichever identity column is
-- actually populated. If emid is ever repopulated it takes precedence again.
--
-- Verified: datetype literal 'Day' (SDS-767, SDS-938); team literal 'Frontline'
-- (confirmed by the same diagnostic: 52,282 Day rows, 20,599 active, 1 day stale).

WITH latest_snapshot AS (
  SELECT MAX(date) AS snapshot_date
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
  WHERE datetype = 'Day'
    AND date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
                 AND CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix')
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    t.*,
    s.snapshot_date,
    -- First non-blank identity value wins
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(t.emid AS STRING)), ''),
      NULLIF(LOWER(TRIM(CAST(t.emailaddress AS STRING))), ''),
      NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(t.username AS STRING)), ''),
      NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(t.employee AS STRING)), '')
    ) AS employee_key
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` AS t
  CROSS JOIN latest_snapshot AS s
  WHERE t.datetype = 'Day'
    AND t.date = s.snapshot_date
    AND t.stillatwayfair IS TRUE
    -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> FRONTLINE SCOPE <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
    -- Verified populated sibling teams, if you want to widen:
    --   'Frontline Training', 'CARE', 'CAT',
    --   'Customer Service Outreach', 'Service Security Team'
    AND t.team IN ('Frontline')
    -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> END SCOPE <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
)
SELECT
  -- Resolved identifier: emid when present, else email/username/name
  b.employee_key                                                  AS `Employee ID`,
  -- `employee` is stored "Last, First" (verified in SDS-938)
  TRIM(COALESCE(REGEXP_EXTRACT(TRIM(CAST(b.employee AS STRING)), r',\s*(.+)$'), '')) AS `Preferred First Name`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(REGEXP_EXTRACT(TRIM(CAST(b.employee AS STRING)), r'^([^,]+)'), ''))   AS `Preferred Last Name`,
  LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.emailaddress AS STRING), '')))       AS `Email Address`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.username AS STRING), ''))                  AS `Sam Account Name`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.site AS STRING), ''))                      AS `Office Location`,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', SAFE_CAST(b.hiredate AS DATE)), '') AS `Start Date`,
  CAST(b.hierarchylevel AS STRING)                                AS `Level`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.team AS STRING), ''))                      AS `Team`,
  CAST(b.wgid AS STRING)                                          AS `Work Group ID`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.workgroup AS STRING), ''))                 AS `Work Group`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.parentworkgroup AS STRING), ''))           AS `Parent Work Group`,
  CAST(b.mgremid AS STRING)                                       AS `Manager's Employee ID`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.manager AS STRING), ''))                   AS `Manager's Name`,
  LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.mgremailaddress AS STRING), '')))    AS `Manager's Email`,
  CAST(b.mgr2emid AS STRING)                                      AS `2nd Level Manager's Employee ID`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.manager2 AS STRING), ''))                  AS `2nd Level Manager's Name`,
  CAST(b.srmgremid AS STRING)                                     AS `Senior Manager's Employee ID`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(b.srmanager AS STRING), ''))                 AS `Senior Manager's Name`,
  CAST(b.snapshot_date AS STRING)                                 AS `Snapshot Date`
FROM base AS b
WHERE b.employee_key IS NOT NULL
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b.employee_key ORDER BY b.lastrundate DESC) = 1
ORDER BY `Manager's Name`, `Preferred Last Name`, `Preferred First Name`

-- Runs ONLY when the roster query returns zero rows.
-- Counts NON-NULL values per column on the newest Frontline 'Day' snapshot, so
-- the exact dead columns are named instead of guessed at. COUNT(col) ignores
-- NULLs, so a 0 here means the column is entirely empty.
WITH latest_snapshot AS (
  SELECT MAX(date) AS snapshot_date
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
  WHERE datetype = 'Day'
    AND date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*)                  AS total_rows,
  COUNT(t.emid)             AS emid,
  COUNT(t.employee)         AS employee,
  COUNT(t.name)             AS name,
  COUNT(t.username)         AS username,
  COUNT(t.emailaddress)     AS emailaddress,
  COUNT(t.swapid)           AS swapid,
  COUNT(t.hierarchylevel)   AS hierarchylevel,
  COUNT(t.hiredate)         AS hiredate,
  COUNT(t.site)             AS site,
  COUNT(t.wgid)             AS wgid,
  COUNT(t.workgroup)        AS workgroup,
  COUNT(t.parentworkgroup)  AS parentworkgroup,
  COUNT(t.mgremid)          AS mgremid,
  COUNT(t.manager)          AS manager,
  COUNT(t.mgremailaddress)  AS mgremailaddress,
  COUNT(t.mgr2emid)         AS mgr2emid,
  COUNT(t.manager2)         AS manager2,
  COUNT(t.srmgremid)        AS srmgremid,
  COUNT(t.srmanager)        AS srmanager
FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` AS t
CROSS JOIN latest_snapshot AS s
WHERE t.datetype = 'Day'
  AND t.date = s.snapshot_date
  AND t.stillatwayfair IS TRUE
  AND t.team IN ('Frontline')

## Frontline Roster - Weekly Monday 4AM Arizona

### Columns were CUT, not left blank
csn_hr is not accessible with this credential, so every Org Browser column that only lives there has been removed. The workflow now writes its own header row containing only what it can actually fill.

REMOVED (18): HRIS ID, Phone Extension, Seniority Date, Forecast End Date, Birthday, Home Department, Employee Type, Headcount Classification, Employee Profile, Job Title, Manager's HRIS ID, Manager's Work Group, 2nd Level Manager's HRIS ID, Reporting VP, Reporting Senior VP, Shirt Size, Term Date, Work Group 1-10 and Work Group 20.

Also removed: the duplicated Preferred First Name / Preferred Last Name columns. They were an Org Browser CSV quirk and identical in every row of your exports.

KEPT (20): Employee ID, Preferred First Name, Preferred Last Name, Email Address, Sam Account Name, Office Location, Start Date, Level, Team, Work Group ID, Work Group, Parent Work Group, Manager's Employee ID, Manager's Name, Manager's Email, 2nd Level Manager's Employee ID, 2nd Level Manager's Name, Senior Manager's Employee ID, Senior Manager's Name, Snapshot Date.

Manager's Email and the two Senior Manager columns are additions - the manager-chain columns are the ones this table populates most reliably, so they are worth having.

This workflow REPLACES row 1. Your pasted 45-column header row will be overwritten with these 17.

### Source
`wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` - employee/day grain with the manager chain denormalized per row, so no join is needed. This is the table your original workflow already had working credentials for.

### emid is NULL in this table - important
A diagnostic run on 2026-09-11 showed COUNT(DISTINCT emid) = 0 across all 128,694 'Day' rows. The emid column exists but is empty for every row. An earlier version filtered on emid IS NOT NULL and so returned nothing.

The employee key is now COALESCE(emid, emailaddress, username, employee) - first non-blank wins - so the roster works whichever identity column is populated, and prefers emid again if it is ever backfilled. The `Employee ID` column contains that resolved value.

If the run still returns zero rows, the failure branch profiles non-NULL counts for every identity and org column and labels each DEAD or ok, so the empty columns are named rather than guessed. Send that output back.

### Scope - verified
`team IN ('Frontline')` is confirmed correct: 52,282 'Day' rows, 20,599 active, 1 day stale as of 2026-09-11. Expect roughly 20k rows.

Verified sibling teams you can add to the SCOPE block: 'Frontline Training', 'CARE', 'CAT', 'Customer Service Outreach', 'Service Security Team'. A large group of rows carries a NULL team and is excluded.

### Safety
Zero rows means the sheet is NOT cleared and the run fails with that diagnosis. A bad filter can never blank the sheet.

The query takes the newest daily snapshot within 30 days rather than hard-coding yesterday, so a missing weekend snapshot does not produce an empty run. The window is deliberately narrow - widening it would publish stale data as current.

### Schedule
Workflow timezone `America/Phoenix`, cron `0 4 * * 1`. Arizona skips DST so this is 11:00 UTC year-round. Confirm the timezone in Workflow Settings after import.

### After import
Select your BigQuery and Google Sheets credentials on the four credentialed nodes, run manually once, check the summary node for employee_row_count and teams_present, then activate.
